votes.reasoning: PercentText.whole is Int(saturating: percent.rounded()). Every call site the diff touches is a label only: notification title, tooltip, menu bar, pinned badge, analytics, sparkline and row views. Threshold decisions (SeverityColor.tint and showsFlame, tracker.crossings `percent >= $0`, `maxPercent > currentPercent + 5`) still read the raw Double. So rounding never changes whether a notification fires or which color is used. Behaviour changes only on screen: the notification title, analytics totalUsagePercent and peakDay used to truncate and now round. AnalyticsView used `%.0f` (ties to even) and now uses .rounded() (ties away from zero), for example 0.5% now shows as 1%. That is display only. Reversal: with the title back on Int(saturating:), NotificationTitleLocalizationTests.swift:42 went RED ('92%' vs '93%').

New file PercentText.swift: one rounding rule, with 4 tests. It replaces about 15 copies of Int(saturating: x.rounded()) plus 3 sites that truncated (notification title, AnalyticsFormatters.peakDayText, VendorAnalyticsCardView). A grep finds no copies left in Sources/AiTaskbarApp. Cosmetic only: most call sites still write "\(PercentText.whole(x))%" where PercentText.format(x) would fit (PinnedStatusItemManager.swift:258,261,271; MenuBarLabelView.swift:414; ProviderRowView.swift:436; SparklineView.swift:449). Not worth another round.

PercentText.swift is new, internal, App-only, and has tests. All 11 changed call sites are Text or String rendering: MenuBarTooltipBuilder, PinnedStatusBadgeView, MenuBarLabelView, ProviderRowView, SparklineView, VendorSectionView, AnalyticsView, AnalyticsFormatters, VendorAnalyticsCardView, and the notification title. The decision paths keep raw Doubles: SeverityColor.showsFlame/tint and the tracker's percent >= threshold. VendorSnapshot and the golden tests are untouched. notif_title_fmt uses %d in en, pt-BR and es, and PercentText.whole still returns Int, so no Localizable change is needed. Only four sites change their displayed value: title, peakDayText and totalUsagePercent went from truncating to rounding, and AnalyticsView went from %.0f to rounding half away from zero. That is the intended alignment. A grep finds no remaining ad-hoc percent formatting in AiTaskbarApp.
